source_binding.mechanism: multi-view consistency using deliberately distinct feature partitions, reduced from co-training's two-view representation concept

public_sources.claim_used: Blum and Mitchell formulate examples as having two distinct feature views and train/use the views separately; their theory assumes each view is sufficient and uses both views together.

Multi-view/co-training methods exploit disagreement or consistency between classifications based on different characterizations of the same samples; strong theoretical guarantees rely on assumptions such as useful views and conditional independence.

source_binding.literal_external_runtime_reason: No co-training implementation, model training, external classifier, hosted service, cloud compute, or user execution is accepted. Public sources supply only the concept of distinct feature views and cross-view consistency.
source_binding.chat_native_reduction: Use two predeclared feature-disjoint views: control-path fields and outcome/recovery fields. Require the same supported anomaly core under both. A renamed copy or overlapping projection is not a second view; disagreement blocks activation, and view definitions cannot be tuned after outcomes in the same generation. No claim of statistical conditional independence is made.

scope_limit: Constructed two-view role-local trace only. Disjoint hand-selected feature sets do not prove conditional independence or freedom from common designer bias.
unresolved_child: Both disjoint views can still be shaped by the same designer. A later leaf should test predeclared perturbation/counterexample pressure on the candidate taxonomy rather than adding another hand-selected descriptive view.

quota_cost_assessment.repository_transport_note: Repository API is lightweight state/evidence transport only; rate-limit interruption is checkpoint/retryable and API volume is not used as compute.
